title: terraform: refactor private GPU node-pools, IAM, networking, and state layout
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Refactor the Terraform modules used by Private deployments to improve flexibility for GPU node pools, unify IAM role definitions, and adopt a safer state layout that supports per-environment state keys. Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated environments require predictable node pool sizing, support for multiple GPU SKUs, and simpler IAM surface area. Operationally we also need to migrate from a single monolithic remote state key to a per-env prefix to enable safer concurrent updates and easier rollbacks. This PR bundles the module refactor, docs updates, and a state migration helper to minimize operational risk.

Changes: - New modules/gpu/node_pool module: supports accelerator_type, accelerator_count, taints/tolerations, node labels, and drainage lifecycle hooks. Replaces bespoke node pool blocks in examples. - IAM consolidation: modules/iam/roles.tf consolidates workload and control-plane role definitions and standardizes assume_roles and policy attachments to reduce drift. - Networking: modules/network/vpc.tf exposes subnetwork tagging for Private installs and tightens default security group egress rules. - State layout: backend.tf now supports a configurable state_prefix (env/${var.env_name}) and includes migration plan guidance. Added a state-migration script (scripts/terraform_state_migrate.sh) that performs a safe state copy with verification steps. - Examples and docs: updated examples/private-deploy/ and docs/terraform/private-deploy.md with migration steps and a rollback checklist. - Tests: added basic unit/format checks and a CI plan validation job that runs terraform validate and a dry-run plan against a ci workspace.

Notes: The description below contains the full context and proposed rollback/migration steps; operators should read the docs before applying to production.

review_conversation: Kenji Watanabe (reviewer): This addresses a lot of longstanding pain points. Main concern is the state migration - can we guarantee no downtime for existing private installs? Please add a clear migration script and a rollback plan.

Aisha Patel (author): Added scripts/terraform_state_migrate.sh with a verification step that compares state SHA before switching state key. Migration guidance documented in docs/terraform/private-deploy.md. The migration is designed to be non-destructive and reversible; operators must run it during a maintenance window.

Lina Gomez (reviewer): IAM consolidation looks good but please ensure we don't break cross-account assume_role patterns used by one customer. Suggest adding outputs for role ARNs and a compatibility toggle.
Aisha Patel: Added role_arn outputs and a var.iam_compat_mode to preserve previous behavior when set. Documented the compatibility toggle in the migration guide.
Rahul Iyer (reviewer): CI failed fmt on first run. Also add an acceptance test for a minimal plan to detect missing required variables.
Aisha Patel: Fixed formatting issues and added a lightweight plan validation job to CI that runs terraform init/validate and a non-destructive plan against a CI workspace. All green now.
merge_outcome: Merged by Kenji Watanabe using squash merge. Commit message consolidated. Merge occurred after 2 approvals and green CI. Post-merge: created a follow-up issue ENG-4187 to monitor any state-migration issues and to run a staged rollout across existing private customers.

Change: Consolidated IAM role definitions and added role_arn outputs and compat toggle
Change: Backend state layout now supports configurable state_prefix (env-scoped keys). Includes migration helper script and operator guide
Docs: Updated private-deploy docs with migration and rollback checklist
CI: Added terraform fmt/validate and dry-run plan job to the pipeline
